subject: Science
title: Science Exam 2
topic: Health & Lifestyle · Periodic Table · Investigative skills
intro: Write in full sentences. Question 7 is a 6-mark answer: plan it in order and use science words.

questions.q: What is the main job of carbohydrates in the diet?
options: Keeping food moving through the gut

questions.q: Which test shows that a food contains lipids (fats)?
options: Ethanol gives a cloudy white emulsion
questions.ms: Ethanol emulsion test: cloudy white layer.

questions.q: Explain why a person with too little iron in their diet may feel tired.
questions.ms: 1 iron is needed to make haemoglobin / red blood cells; 1 so less oxygen is carried, less respiration, less energy released.

questions.q: Describe two health problems that can be caused by eating too much fat and sugar over a long time. Explain how one of them happens.
questions.ms: 1 each for two problems: obesity, heart disease, type 2 diabetes, tooth decay, high blood pressure; 1 explanation, e.g. fat builds up in arteries so less blood reaches the heart, or more energy eaten than used is stored as fat.

questions.q: Explain how bacteria in the large intestine help the body.
questions.ms: Any 2: break down substances we can't digest (fibre); make vitamins (e.g. vitamin K); compete with / stop harmful bacteria growing.

questions.q: Enzymes are described as biological catalysts. Explain what this means, using protease as an example.
questions.ms: 1 speed up reactions; 1 not used up / can be used again; 1 protease breaks proteins down into amino acids.

questions.q: Describe what happens to a piece of bread as it travels from the mouth to the end of the small intestine. Include what happens to the starch in the bread.
questions.ms: Level 3 (5–6): clear ordered journey with enzymes and absorption. Level 2 (3–4): most stages, some detail. Level 1 (1–2): a few correct points. Points: teeth chew into smaller pieces / larger surface area; saliva contains amylase; amylase breaks starch into sugar (maltose); swallowed down oesophagus by peristalsis; stomach churns, acid kills bacteria; small intestine: enzymes from pancreas finish digestion to glucose; glucose absorbed into blood through villi.

questions.q: Explain one way that drinking too much alcohol harms the body.
questions.ms: 1 effect: damages liver / slows the nervous system / addictive; 1 consequence: liver disease (cirrhosis), slower reactions so more accidents, dependence.

questions.q: Which element is in Group 7 and Period 2?
Which property is typical of a solid non-metal?
Give two physical properties of Group 1 metals that are different from most other metals.
questions.ms: Any 2: soft (can be cut with a knife); low density (float on water); low melting points.

questions.ms: 1 melting point increases down the group; 1 data quoted, e.g. fluorine −220 °C to iodine 114 °C.

questions.q: Iodine solution is added to sodium chloride solution. Predict what happens and explain your answer.
questions.ms: 1 no reaction / no displacement; 1 iodine is less reactive than chlorine (lower in Group 7).

questions.q: Argon is used inside some light bulbs. Explain why, using its position in the Periodic Table.
questions.ms: 1 argon is in Group 0 / a noble gas so it is unreactive (full outer shell); 1 so the hot filament does not react / burn.

questions.q: Josh investigates how temperature affects how quickly the enzyme amylase breaks down starch. Name the independent variable, the dependent variable and two control variables.
questions.ms: 1 IV temperature; 1 DV time for starch to be broken down (iodine no longer turns blue-black); 2 controls: volume/concentration of amylase, volume/concentration of starch, pH.

questions.q: Josh's times were 34 s, 36 s, 62 s and 35 s. The 62 s result is anomalous. Calculate the mean time, leaving out the anomaly.
Which type of graph should you use to show the number of students in a class choosing each favourite food?
Explain why scientists repeat their readings.
questions.ms: 1 to spot anomalous results; 1 to calculate a mean / make results more repeatable (reliable).
